Open-source Python library · built for health data

Synthetic patients who add up to a real population.

meddies-faker generates fake people and patients from published census, survey and hospital statistics. Age, region, ethnicity, insurance, diagnosis, IDs and addresses agree with each other, and every value can tell you which table it came from. Test health software, train de-identification models and teach without a single real patient record.

pip install "meddies-faker[vn]"

    Healthcare

    Patients without patient data.

    Clinical text is full of identifiers: names, birth dates, record numbers, insurance cards, hospitals, diagnoses. meddies-faker writes realistic patient documents with every identifier labelled, so a de-identification model can learn from text that never belonged to anyone.

        Statistics

        Generate 100,000 people and you get the country back.

        Every pack benchmarked on 100,000 profiles against its own national tables, next to the same number of records from Faker's locale for that country where one exists. The deviation is the share of probability that differs from the source (0 % is identical); sampling noise is what a perfect sampler of the same size still shows.

          Principles

          Built like a statistics office, shipped like a library.

          Every number has a source

          Each table carries its publisher, locator and retrieval date; estimates are marked and explained. No unsourced figures.

          Faithful by default

          Populations such as inpatients and tail controls act at sampling time and never rewrite the sourced tables.

          Deterministic and offline

          Same seed, same people. No network at runtime; runtime dependencies are pydantic and PyYAML.

          No real identifiers

          IDs are structurally valid and consistent with the person, never a real person's number.

          Contribute

          Open source, and only as good as its sources.

          meddies-faker is being opened to the community. The most valuable help is a better figure with a citable source: an official table that replaces an estimate. Clinicians, statisticians, health researchers and developers all have something to add.

          Bring a better source

          Know the official table behind an estimate (a census table, a ministry report, a statute)? Open a New data source issue with the link and page.

          Report a wrong figure

          A value that differs from its cited source, or a document format that hospitals in your country write differently.

          Add a country or a field

          A country is one directory of sourced tables; a field is one YAML file. Both guides walk through a complete example.
